question: In July 2017, India's first solar-powered train was launched from the railway station of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Delhi__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's first solar-powered train** was launched from Delhi's Safdarjung railway station on July 14, 2017.
 
• The train** was a diesel-electric multiple unit (DEMU**) that ran from Safdarjung Station to Farukh Nagar in Haryana
 
• The train has six trailer coaches, with 16 solar panels fitted in each of them.
 
• The solar panels will power all the electrical appliances inside.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Noida-based firm Jakson Engineers Limited (JEL) had been given the task of providing solar panels for DEMU coaches set to be used by the Railways for its pilot projects in Chennai and Amritsar.
 
• Indian Railway's first DEMU service was launched from Jalandhar to Hoshiarpur in 1994. 
 
• It will reduce CO2 emissions by 9 tonnes per coach per annum.
 
• The **train also had a battery backup that could run for at least 72 hours**. 
 
• The **solar panels were made under the "Make in India" initiative. **
 
• The train was expected to save the railways money and reduce carbon dioxide emissions.
